response: Patient-Controlled Therapy (PCT) of breathlessness in palliative care is a feasible and acceptable therapeutic method for reducing refractory breathlessness in patients. This approach involves the administration of opioids, which has been shown to be effective in managing breathlessness in palliative care patients. The use of PCT allows patients to have control over their opioid administration, which can help to improve their symptoms and quality of life. This therapeutic concept is a valuable addition to the management of breathlessness in palliative care, providing patients with a sense of control and relief from their symptoms.
